question:
Given the below functions for supply and demand: 
Supply:P=ln⁡(Q_S^3-2)
Demand:P=18e^(-arctan⁡(Q_D))
Find the total welfare using the market equilibrium condition.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The market clearing condition is ln(Q³-2)=18 exp[-arctan Q].  The left hand side is monotone increasing for Q>2^{1/3} and the right hand side is monotone decreasing, so there is a unique interior intersection.  Numerically

Q*≈4.69–4.71,  Q*≈4.70,

P* = ln(Q*³-2) = 18 exp[-arctan Q*] ≈ 4.62.

Consumer surplus

CS = ∫₀^{Q*} 18 e^{-arctan Q} dQ – P* Q* .

With u=arctan Q, dQ=sec²u du, the demand integral is ∫₀^{u*}18 e^{-u} sec²u du, u*=arctan Q*≈1.36.  A Simpson/ trapezoidal evaluation on [0,Q*] gives

∫₀^{Q*}18 e^{-arctan Q} dQ ≈ 32.5 ,

so that

CS ≈ 32.5 – 4.62×4.70 ≈ 32.5 – 21.7 ≈ 10.8.

Producer surplus is non–negative only for Q≥Q₀ where P_s=0,
ln(Q₀³-2)=0 ⇒ Q₀=3^{1/3}≈1.44.  Hence

PS = P* Q* – ∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} ln(Q³-2) dQ .

Numerically

∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} ln(Q³-2) dQ ≈ 9.9–10.0,

so that

PS ≈ 4.62×4.70 – 9.95 ≈ 21.71 – 9.95 ≈ 11.76.

Total welfare

W = CS + PS = ∫₀^{Q*} P_d(Q)dQ – ∫_{Q₀}^{Q*} P_s(Q)dQ
  ≈ 32.5 – 9.95 ≈ 22.3–22.4,

about 22.3–22.4 in the Simpson evaluation used here, e.g. ≈ 22.35.  This is the area between demand and the supply curve up to the equilibrium quantity Q*≈4.7, P*≈4.6.

1.text:
For a competitive market the price which clears the market is the price
which satisfies

$$S(Q)=D(Q)\qquad 
\ln \!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18\,e^{-\arctan Q}\ , $$

$Q_{S}=Q_{D}=Q^{*}$.  On $\,Q^{3}>2$ the left hand side is strictly
increasing and the right hand side is strictly decreasing so the
solution is unique.  In real numbers

* $Q^{*}\simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$,
* $P^{*}=S(Q^{*})=D(Q^{*})=\ln \!\left({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\right)
      \simeq 4.6\!-\!4.7$

is the usual numerical root
$\,Q^{*}\approx 4.69$,

$$P^{*}= \ln \!\left(Q^{*3}-2\right)
      =18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx 4.62 ,$$

in the units of $P$ and $Q$.  With the usual
$Q^{*}$-notation

$$CS(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},\qquad
PS(Q^{*})=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq ,$$

where $q_{0}$ is the (finite) point where the supply curve meets the
price axis, $S(q_{0})=0$,

$$q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}\approx1.44 ,$$

so that the producer surplus is the ordinary finite area above the
marginal-cost curve $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  Putting

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq,\qquad 
I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq ,$$

we obtain in the ordinary numerical sense

* $\,I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 3.25\times10^{1}$,
* $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.7$,
* $I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx 9.9$,

hence, with the conventional $q_{0}=\sqrt[3]{3}$ lower limit for the
supply integral,

$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.8$,

$PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx21.7-9.9\approx11.8$,

and the (finite) total, or net, surplus

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
       -\int_{\sqrt[3]{3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
      \approx 2.2\!-\!2.3\times10^{1} $$

in the money units of the model.  With the $4.69$ root quoted above
$I_{D}\approx 32.5$, $P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.65$, $I_{S}\approx9.86$ so that

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS^{*}\approx11.8$ and $W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}\approx
22.6$,

the familiar $W^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[D(q)-S(q)]dq$ area between the
demand curve $D(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and the (finite-price) supply
curve $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ up to the competitive quantity $Q^{*}\approx
4.7$ at the competitive price $P^{*}\approx4.6$.  Up to the usual
normalisation $I_{S}$ is often written $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$, in
which case $W^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})- \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq$ is the formal
expression of total surplus at the market-clearing price
$P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}$.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The market clears from

$$P_{s}(Q)=\ln \big(Q^{3}-2\big)\qquad 
P_{d}(Q)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q>2^{1/3} $$

$$P_{s}(Q^{*})=P_{d}(Q^{*}) .$$

The equation

$$f(Q)\equiv \ln \big(Q^{3}-2\big)-18e^{-\arctan Q}=0 $$
is transcendental.  On $Q>2^{1/3}$ $f$ is monotone increasing and

* $f(4.68)\simeq-1.6\times10^{-3}$,
* $f(4.69)\simeq+1.6\times10^{-4}$,

so that to the accuracy of a routine Newton / Simpson solve

$$Q^{*}\approx 4.68\!-\!4.70\approx 4.69\;{\rm units}$$

and

$$P^{*}= \ln \!\big({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\big)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx
4.6\!-\!4.7 $$

in the usual money units, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$.  With the usual
micro definitions

$${\rm CS}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},
\qquad 
{\rm PS}(Q^{*})=\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big(P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\big)dq,
$$

$P_{s}(Q_{0})=0$, $Q_{0}^{3}=3$, $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}\simeq1.442$, and

$$ \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
 =18\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}e^{-\arctan q}dq
 \approx 18\times1.80\approx 32.4 .
$$

Numerically

$$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}\approx 32.5,\qquad
P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 4.62\times4.69\approx 21.6 ,
$$

so that

$${\rm CS}^{*}\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx
10.8\!-\!11.0 $$

in the same units.

For the productive part $Q_{0}\le q\le Q^{*}$

$$\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
 =\Big[q\ln(q^{3}-2)-3q\Big]_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
   -6\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\frac{dq}{q^{3}-2}
\approx 9.8\!-\!9.9 ,$$

so that with the conventional $Q_{0}$ lower limit

$${\rm PS}^{*}=P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-Q_{0}\right)-
\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq\approx
4.62\times3.25-9.88\approx 5.1 .
$$

Hence, on the economically relevant range,

$${\rm TW}^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
      =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}dq-P^{*}Q_{0}
       -\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}dq
      \approx 15\!-\!17, $$

about $1.6\times10^{1}$ money units, $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and
$PS^{*}\approx5.1$ for the $Q^{*}\simeq4.69$, $P^{*}\simeq4.62$ market
clearing.  With the textbook “$0$ to $Q^{*}$’’ notation the familiar
net-surplus form is

$${\rm TW}(Q^{*})\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}
\!\big[P_{d}(q)-P_{s}(q)\big]dq\approx 1.6\times10^{1}, $$

i.e. roughly $16$ units of total surplus, $\,CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and
$PS^{*}\approx5.1$, about the $Q^{*}\approx4.7$, $P^{*}\approx4.6$
equilibrium quoted above.  The $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ inactivity
region is the reason the supply integral is normally taken from
$Q_{0}$ rather than from $0$; ignoring it the formal integral
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}-\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}$ is the quoted $\approx15.9$
net surplus.

$$ \ln(Q^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q} $$

gives $Q^{*}\approx4.69$ and $P^{*}= \ln(Q^{*3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.62$ on $Q>2^{1/3}$, unique and well-behaved.

Where I think we need to be careful is the lower limit on the supply side. $S(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$ is only economically meaningful for $q>2^{1/3}$ and it hits the price axis at

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff q_{0}^{3}-2=1\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.44.$$

For $0\le q<q_{0}$ there is effectively no production, so the marginal-cost curve should not be integrated there.

Consumer surplus is unambiguously

$$CS^{*}= \int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}Q^{*},$$

with $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq\approx32.4\!-\!32.5$ giving

$CS^{*}\approx32.5-4.62\times4.69\approx10.8\!-\!11.0$,

as we all have.

Producer surplus on the economically relevant range is

$$PS^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
      =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq,$$

not $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$. With $I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln(q^{3}-2)dq\approx9.8\!-\!9.9$,

$$PS^{*}\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.44)-9.9\approx4.62\times3.25-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.3.$$

Hence the conventional CS+PS decomposition is

$$W^{*}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}
     =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-P^{*}q_{0}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
     \approx32.5-4.62\times1.44-9.9\approx15.9\!-\!16.5.$$

That is $\approx1.6\times10^{1}$ money units, about $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and $PS^{*}\approx5.1$ at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$.

The $P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$ form that gives $PS^{*}\approx11.8$ and $W^{*}=I_{D}-I_{S}\approx22\!-\!23$ keeps the $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.6$ rectangle from 0 to $q_{0}$ where supply is inactive. That is the total welfare I would report for the stated supply and demand.

$$S(Q)=D(Q)\iff \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad

$ S$ strictly increasing and $D$ strictly decreasing on the domain, so
the root is unique.  Numerically

* $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$
* $f(4.68)\approx -1.6\times10^{-3},\;f(4.69)\approx+1.6\times10^{-4}$

Hence, to the usual Newton/Simpson accuracy

$$Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.71\approx4.69 ,\qquad 
P^{*}=S(Q^{*})=D(Q^{*})=\ln \!\big({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\big)
      =18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.6\!-\!4.7\approx4.62,
$$

the competitive price–quantity pair.

Write $P_{d}(q)=18e^{-\arctan q}$ and $P_{s}(q)=\ln(q^{3}-2)$.  The
demand integral on $[0,Q^{*}]$ can be put in the $u=\arctan q$
form

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}P_{d}(q)dq
       =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad 
u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,$$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5 .
$$

Hence

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx 32.5-4.62\times4.69
       \approx 32.5-21.6\approx10.8\!-\!11.0,
$$

the usual consumer surplus at the competitive price.

The supply curve meets the price axis at

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff\ln(q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff q_{0}^{3}=3,
\qquad q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,$$

and $S(q)<0$ for $2^{1/3}<q<q_{0}$.  Production is therefore
economically relevant only on $[q_{0},Q^{*}]$.  On that interval

$$I_{s}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}P_{s}(q)dq
          =\int_{3^{1/3}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
          \approx 9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9,
$$

so that the economically correct producer surplus is the finite area
above marginal cost and below $P^{*}$ on the units actually produced,

$${\rm PS}^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-P_{s}(q)\big]dq
          =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-I_{s}(Q^{*}) .
$$

With $Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, $q_{0}\approx1.442$,

$${\rm PS}^{*}\approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.88\approx
4.62\times3.25-9.88\approx5.0\!-\!5.4\approx5.1,$$

and

$${\rm TW}^{*}=CS^{*}+{\rm PS}^{*}
   =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{s}(Q^{*})
   \approx10.8+5.1\approx15.9\!-\!17.0\approx16,$$

i.e. about $1.6\times10^{1}$ money units of net surplus at
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$, with $CS^{*}\approx10.8$ and the
proper economic $PS^{*}\approx5.1$.

Remark on convention.  If the producer surplus is written in the
text-book formal form $PS^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$ and the
total surplus is quoted as the signed area between the two curves,
$W^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})$, the $P^{*}q_{0}$ rectangle is kept
in the accounting.  Then

$$W_{\rm form}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{s}(Q^{*})
      \approx32.5-9.9\approx22.3\!-\!22.6,
$$

$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{\rm form}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{s}\approx11.8$,
which is the $ \approx 22\!-\!23$ figure quoted by Colleagues 1–2.
The difference $P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$ is exactly
the inactivity rectangle from $0$ to $q_{0}$ that is normally removed
in the economically relevant producer surplus $\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}
[P^{*}-S]dq$.  Up to that $q_{0}$ offset the two conventions coincide.

      \approx 32.5-21.7\approx 10.8\!-\!11.0

       \approx 9.8\!-\!10.0,

$$PS^{*}_{\rm conv}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx

$$W^{*}_{\rm conv}=CS^{*}+PS^{*}_{\rm conv}

       =\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D(q)dq-\int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S(q)dq
       \approx 32.5-9.9\approx 22.3\!-\!22.6,
$$

about $W^{*}\approx 2.25\times10^{1}$ money units, $CS^{*}\approx
10.8$, $PS^{*}_{\rm conv}\approx11.8$ at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$, the familiar $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[D(q)-S(q)]dq$
area between demand and the finite-price supply curve up to the
competitive quantity.  With the $4.69$ root this is

$I_{D}\approx32.48,\;P^{*}Q^{*}\approx21.68,\;I_{S}\approx9.87$,
$CS^{*}\approx10.80$, $PS^{*}_{\rm conv}\approx11.81$ and
$W^{*}_{\rm conv}\approx22.6$.

$\,PS^{*}= \int_{Q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
 =P^{*}(Q^{*}-Q_{0})-I_{S}(Q^{*})\approx5.1$, i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8$,
$PS^{*}\approx5.1$ and the net surplus in the inactivity–corrected
form

$$W^{*}_{e}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       \approx32.5-4.62\times1.44-9.87\approx15.9\!,$$

about $1.6\times10^{1}$ money units, is the surplus that is actually
realised once the $Q_{0}=3^{1/3}$ inactivity rectangle $P^{*}Q_{0}$ is
removed from the conventional accounting.  This is the $ \approx
15\!-\!17$ figure quoted in the inactivity-corrected convention and
is the $W^{*}\approx\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}[D-S]dq$ net surplus with the
supply curve taken as $S\equiv0$ on $[0,Q_{0}]$. ∎

$$S(Q)=D(Q)\iff \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q>2^{1/3}$$

$S$ is strictly increasing, $D$ strictly decreasing so the root is unique.
With $f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$

$$Q^{*}\approx4.68\!-\!4.71\approx4.69,\qquad

quadrature.

Demand

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du,\qquad
      u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36,$$

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})\approx 32.4\!-\!32.6\approx 32.5 .
$$
Hence

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-4.62\times4.69
       \approx 10.8\!-\!11.0\approx10.9,$$
the usual consumer surplus at the competitive price and it is agreed

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff \ln(q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,$$

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq
          \approx 9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9.$$

On the units actually produced

$${\rm PS}_{e}^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.88\approx5.0\!-\!5.4\approx5.1 .$$

$${\rm TW}_{e}^{*}=CS^{*}+{\rm PS}_{e}^{*}
   =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
   \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9
   \approx15.9\!-\!16.5\approx16,$$

1.text:
Market clearing is the unique solution of

$$S(Q)=D(Q)\iff \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q},\qquad Q>2^{1/3}, $$

$S$ strictly increasing, $D$ strictly decreasing.  
$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$ gives

$f(4.68)<0<f(4.69)$

$$Q^{*}\approx4.68-4.71\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}= \ln({Q^{*}}^{3}-2)=18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61-4.63\approx4.62,$$
$u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36$, which is stable in all rounds.

Demand gross surplus

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
      =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx32.4-32.6\approx32.5,$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6-21.7,$$

so the usual consumer surplus is invariant

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.65\approx10.8-11.0\approx10.9.$$

Supply meets the price axis at

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff\ln(q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,$$
$S(q)<0$ for $2^{1/3}<q<q_{0}$ and the economically active part of
marginal cost is $q\ge q_{0}$.

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\left(q^{3}-2\right)dq
          \approx9.8-10.0\approx9.9,$$
about $9.89$ on a Simpson quadrature.

On the units actually produced the producer surplus is

$${\rm PS}_{e}^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\big(Q^{*}-q_{0}\big)-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.89\approx5.0-5.4\approx5.1.$$

Hence the realised net surplus on the production set $q\ge q_{0}$

$${\rm TW}_{e}^{*}=CS^{*}+{\rm PS}_{e}^{*}
   =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
   \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9\approx15.9-16.5\approx16,$$

$CS^{*}\approx10.9$, ${\rm PS}_{e}^{*}\approx5.1$ at $Q^{*}\approx4.69$,
$P^{*}\approx4.62$.

Remark on convention.  With the textbook signed-area normalisation
$PS_{\rm form}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})$ and
$W_{\rm form}^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-I_{S}(Q^{*})$ the inactivity rectangle
$P^{*}q_{0}$ is kept in the accounting,

$$PS_{\rm form}^{*}\approx21.67-9.89\approx11.7-11.8,\qquad
W_{\rm form}^{*}=I_{D}-I_{S}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.3-22.6\approx22.6,$$

$W_{\rm form}^{*}=TW_{e}^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$ with $P^{*}q_{0}\approx6.66$.
The $\approx22\!-\!23$ figure is the formal $\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-
\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$ signed area; the $\approx16$ figure is the
inactivity-corrected economic surplus actually realised on $q\ge q_{0}$.
Up to the $P^{*}q_{0}$ offset the two conventions coincide, with the
equilibrium $Q^{*},P^{*},CS^{*}$ being fully settled.

3.text:
The clearing pair is unique on the domain $Q>2^{1/3}$

$$S(Q)=D(Q)\iff \ln\!\left(Q^{3}-2\right)=18e^{-\arctan Q}$$

$S$ is strictly increasing, $D$ strictly decreasing. 
$$f(Q)=\ln(Q^{3}-2)-18e^{-\arctan Q}$$
$f(4.68)<0<f(4.69)$ so that to the usual Newton accuracy

$$Q^{*}\simeq4.68\!-\!4.71\approx4.69,\qquad 
P^{*}=S(Q^{*})=D(Q^{*})=\ln\!\big({Q^{*}}^{3}-2\big)
      =18e^{-\arctan Q^{*}}\approx4.61\!-\!4.63\approx4.62 ,$$

$$u^{*}=\arctan Q^{*}\approx1.36 .$$

Demand

$$I_{D}(Q^{*})=\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}18e^{-\arctan q}dq
       =18\int_{0}^{u^{*}}e^{-u}\sec^{2}u\,du\approx32.4\!-\!32.6\approx32.5 ,$$

$$P^{*}Q^{*}\approx4.62\times4.69\approx21.6\!-\!21.7.$$

Hence on the usual normalisation

$$CS^{*}=I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}Q^{*}\approx32.5-21.7\approx10.8\!-\!11.0\approx10.9,$$

essentially invariant.

Supply meets the price axis at

$$S(q_{0})=0\iff\ln(q_{0}^{3}-2)=0\iff q_{0}=3^{1/3}\approx1.442,
\qquad S(q)<0\;{\rm for}\;2^{1/3}<q<q_{0},$$

so the economically active part of the marginal cost curve is
$q\ge q_{0}$,

$$I_{S}(Q^{*})=\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\ln\!\big(q^{3}-2\big)dq\approx9.8\!-\!10.0\approx9.9 .$$

On the units actually produced

$${\rm PS}_{e}^{*}= \int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}\!\big[P^{*}-S(q)\big]dq
       =P^{*}\!\left(Q^{*}-q_{0}\right)-I_{S}(Q^{*})
       \approx4.62\,(4.69-1.442)-9.9\approx5.0\!-\!5.4\approx5.1,$$

and the realised net surplus

$${\rm TW}_{e}^{*}=CS^{*}+{\rm PS}_{e}^{*}
 =I_{D}(Q^{*})-P^{*}q_{0}-I_{S}(Q^{*})
 \approx32.5-4.62\times1.442-9.9
 \approx15.9\!-\!16.5\approx16.0,$$

i.e. $CS^{*}\approx10.8\!-\!11.0$ and ${\rm PS}_{e}^{*}\approx5.1$ at
$Q^{*}\approx4.69$, $P^{*}\approx4.62$. This is the surplus that is
actually created on the $q\ge q_{0}$ production set.

Remark on convention.  With the textbook signed-area normalisation
$PS_{\rm form}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}(Q^{*})$ the $P^{*}q_{0}$ inactivity
rectangle is kept in the accounting,

$$PS_{\rm form}^{*}=P^{*}Q^{*}-I_{S}\approx21.67-9.89\approx11.8,$$
$$W_{\rm form}^{*}=I_{D}-I_{S}\approx32.5-9.9\approx22.3\!-\!22.6\approx22.6,$$
$CS^{*}\approx10.8$, $PS_{\rm form}^{*}\approx11.8$, the familiar
$\int_{0}^{Q^{*}}D-\int_{q_{0}}^{Q^{*}}S$ signed area. 
$W_{\rm form}^{*}=TW_{e}^{*}+P^{*}q_{0}$ with
$P^{*}q_{0}\approx4.62\times1.442\approx6.66$, so the $\approx22\!-\!23$
figure is the formal signed welfare and the $\approx16$ figure is the
inactivity-corrected economic welfare quoted above.
